finding: Risk function learning exists: late L improves overall latent RMSE and coverage, largely through high-frequency tasks. Ordinary compatible and separate-head latent means still regress. A known family does not remove these losses. Environmental variance mean bias is small relative to its scale and does not identify a scalar correction.
metric_scope: Full unqueried-bank latent predictions differ from adaptive next-query density and from decision loss. Late population gains do not override A37 source-gate failures or establish acquisition/recommendation benefits.
next_hypothesis: Retain source-task sparse function variance directions as an empirical distribution rather than pooling them inside ordinary/high-frequency classes. Compare to the exact moment-collapsed covariance and per-task same-scale isotropic controls. This tests source-learned support co-occurrence; do not increase a fitted frequency-class count or use true supports.
